ideas.name: Deep LSTM sequence transduction
ideas.description: Separate multilayer LSTM networks encode a source sentence and autoregressively decode a target sentence, allowing the recurrent language-model decoder to be conditioned on an encoded source at large translation scale.

uncertainties.note: The proceedings target says it uses Graves’s LSTM formulation. The atlas records documented LSTM and recurrent-language-model ancestry without treating the target as an implementation of every earlier equation.

ideas.name: Source-sequence reversal for shorter dependencies
ideas.description: Reversing source-token order while retaining ordinary target order creates several short source-to-target computational paths, reducing the minimum lag without changing average aligned-token distance.

uncertainties.note: The measured reversal intervention and the authors’ incomplete causal explanation remain separate. Reversal is not bidirectionality, attention, or backward target generation.

ideas.name: Differentiable external-memory read
ideas.description: A query scores separately stored memory keys, a softmax turns those scores into a distribution over slots, and the weighted sum of corresponding values remains differentiable from the final task loss.

uncertainties.note: The query, input-memory vectors, and output-memory vectors are structurally comparable to query, key, and value roles, but the source calls the mechanism recurrent attention over external memory rather than Transformer self-attention.

ideas.name: Multi-hop memory retrieval
ideas.description: A retrieved value updates an internal query or state before another soft read, allowing a fixed number of retrieval-and-update steps before the externally visible prediction.

uncertainties.note: The reported aggregate trend favors multiple reads, but adding a hop does not improve every task or perplexity row monotonically.

ideas.name: Memory position and time encoding
ideas.description: Within-sentence position coefficients and learned memory-age embeddings preserve word order and relative story time that an unordered bag of stored symbols would otherwise discard.

uncertainties.note: This paper’s position encoding is attached to explicit memory records and is not evidence for inheritance of the Transformer’s sinusoidal sequence-position representation.

ideas.name: Memory-read neural language model
ideas.description: Recent words occupy explicit memory slots, and repeated content-addressed reads update a recurrent state before a vocabulary softmax predicts the next word.

uncertainties.note: The language-model application first appears in arXiv version 4; it is not transferred into the QA-only first three revisions.

ideas.name: Multiplicative cross-attention scoring
ideas.description: A decoder state scores encoder states with an unparameterized dot product or a learned bilinear form before softmax normalization and a source-side weighted sum.

uncertainties.note: Luong’s score is unscaled and evaluated inside recurrent encoder–decoder attention. Technical continuity with scaled batched QKᵀ does not establish that the Transformer authors adopted the mechanism from this paper.

ideas.name: Local windowed cross-attention
ideas.description: The decoder restricts source attention to a fixed-width neighborhood around a monotonic or learned position, trading a full-source scan for a differentiable local view.

uncertainties.note: The five-BLEU headline includes score choice and input feeding; the isolated transition from the reported global-plus-feed row to local-p/general-plus-feed is 0.9 BLEU.

ideas.name: Attentional input feeding
ideas.description: The previous attentional output is concatenated with the next decoder input so subsequent recurrent states can condition on earlier source-attention decisions.

uncertainties.note: The paper presents input feeding as an alignment-history or coverage-like aid, not as a measured guarantee that every source position is translated exactly once.

ideas.name: Recurrent intra-attention memory tape
ideas.description: At each recurrent step, the current input and prior adaptive state score earlier hidden states; one soft distribution reads aligned summaries from hidden and memory tapes, and those summaries feed the next gated state update.

uncertainties.note: The source calls this intra-attention inside a left-to-right recurrent model. The atlas keeps it distinct from recurrence-free all-position self-attention.

ideas.name: Gated inter–intra attention fusion
ideas.description: A two-sequence model combines attention over the target’s earlier states with attention over an encoded source; shallow fusion keeps those modules separate, while deep fusion gates the source summary into recurrent target memory.

ideas.name: Decomposable cross-sentence attention
ideas.description: Shared feed-forward projections score every element pair across two sequences; a softmax in each direction creates a separately aligned phrase for every element without a recurrent or convolutional encoder in the core model.

ideas.name: Attend–compare–aggregate factorization
ideas.description: Soft alignment decomposes a sentence-pair decision into independent aligned-subphrase comparisons; summing the resulting comparison vectors yields a fixed-size input for the final classifier.

ideas.name: Distance-biased feed-forward intra-attention
ideas.description: Feed-forward projections score all pairs within one sentence, learned relative-distance buckets bias the softmax, and each word is concatenated with its self-aligned phrase while position-wise computation remains parallel.

uncertainties.note: The target names Cheng’s intra-sentence-attention concept but replaces Cheng’s sequential gated tape with all-pairs feed-forward self-alignment and a relative-distance bias; the lineage edge is therefore concept-level, not equation identity.

ideas.name: Masked convolutional autoregressive decoding
ideas.description: A one-dimensional decoder convolution hides future target positions so every output distribution depends only on the permitted prefix, while all training positions can be evaluated together.

uncertainties.note: The mask permits position-wise parallel computation during training; autoregressive target generation still advances one output position at a time.

ideas.name: Dilated convolutional sequence transduction
ideas.description: Repeated one-dimensional convolutions use increasing dilation to widen a fixed-depth receptive field and shorten distant signal paths while preserving convolutional computation across sequence positions.

uncertainties.note: ByteNet directly credits earlier masking, dilation, residual, normalization, WaveNet, and Video Pixel Network mechanisms; this idea records their transduction combination without assigning ByteNet sole priority for those components.

ideas.name: Resolution-preserving dynamic unfolding
ideas.description: A decoder is stacked position-wise over an encoder representation whose width scales with the source, then unfolds until an end symbol so unequal source and target lengths do not require one fixed source vector.

uncertainties.note: Version 1 aligns the representation width with the source and zero-pads the current aligned encoder column beyond it; version 2 instead estimates an extended representation width. The shared idea does not erase that material implementation change.

ideas.name: Contiguous convolutional sequence transduction
ideas.description: Stacked fixed-width, stride-one convolutions replace sequence-aligned recurrent state updates in both encoder and causal decoder, growing the receptive field by k − 1 positions per layer while preserving training-time parallelism across positions.

uncertainties.note: ConvS2S uses contiguous kernels rather than ByteNet-style dilation; its long-distance path remains linear in sequence length for fixed kernel width.

ideas.name: Learned absolute sequence-position embeddings
ideas.description: A learned vector indexed by absolute source or target position is added to each token embedding so nonrecurrent sequence computation can distinguish order and position.

uncertainties.note: ConvS2S uses learned absolute positions but does not claim their invention; Transformer later tests this cited alternative while retaining sinusoidal positions as its canonical default.

ideas.name: Layerwise multi-step cross-attention
ideas.description: Each decoder layer makes its own normalized source read, and the resulting conditional summary enters later decoder-layer computation so successive layers can refine the source evidence before prediction.

uncertainties.note: The paper calls these multiple attention hops, but they are encoder–decoder reads distributed across convolutional decoder layers, not Transformer-style self-attention.

ideas.name: Self-attention sequence mixing
ideas.description: Each sequence position forms a content-dependent weighted combination of representations from other permitted positions in the same sequence, allowing global position-to-position communication without a sequence-aligned recurrent update or nontrivial-width convolution.

uncertainties.note: The work cites earlier self- or intra-attention applications and attention-only entailment models. This idea names the Transformer’s sequence-mixing role without claiming that the paper originated self-attention.
The decoder mask prevents access to later target positions during prediction; it does not make complete autoregressive generation parallel across output steps.

ideas.name: Scaled dot-product attention
ideas.description: Query–key dot products are divided by the square root of key dimension before a softmax weights the values, limiting score scale while retaining a matrix-multiplication implementation.

uncertainties.note: The variance calculation motivates the scale under an independence/unit-variance assumption. The paper does not isolate the scaling factor in a dedicated reported ablation.

ideas.name: Multi-head attention
ideas.description: Several learned query, key, and value projections run attention in parallel; their outputs are concatenated and projected again so one layer can form multiple lower-dimensional retrieval views.

uncertainties.note: The single-head development result and selected visualizations support a bounded empirical description; they do not prove that heads always specialize, remain independent, or yield faithful explanations.

ideas.name: Position encoding without recurrence
ideas.description: Position-dependent vectors are added to token embeddings so an architecture without recurrent or nontrivial-width convolutional sequence order can distinguish and relate token positions.

uncertainties.note: Sinusoidal and learned positions have nearly equal in-distribution development scores in the reported row; the hypothesized advantage for extrapolating beyond training lengths is not tested.

ideas.name: Attention path length and within-layer parallelism
ideas.description: Layer families are compared by asymptotic work, the minimum sequential operations within a layer, and the longest computational path between positions, exposing a tradeoff between global quadratic attention and recurrent or convolutional paths.

uncertainties.note: Table 1 is an analytic comparison. It does not by itself establish hardware speed, memory use, learned dependency quality, or faster autoregressive decoding.

ideas.name: Bidirectional language-model pretraining
ideas.description: Separate forward and backward autoregressive language models are trained together, allowing transferred token features to incorporate both earlier and later sentence context without treating the two directions as one normalized joint likelihood.

ideas.name: Deep contextual token representations
ideas.description: Each token occurrence is represented by the context-independent input layer and every internal layer of a pretrained sequence model, so its transferred vector can vary with sentence context and expose several abstraction levels.

ideas.name: Task-specific pretrained-layer mixture
ideas.description: A downstream task learns normalized scalar weights over pretrained layers plus a task scale, choosing a different mixture of transferred representations without changing the pretrained network.

ideas.name: Feature-based language-model transfer
ideas.description: A pretrained language model remains frozen while its token-level states are supplied as learned features to a separately supervised task architecture.

ideas.name: Character-aware contextual token representation
ideas.description: A character-composed, context-independent token vector feeds recurrent contextual layers, combining subword-form information with sentence-conditioned representations.

ideas.name: Target-domain language-model adaptation
ideas.description: A generally pretrained language model receives an additional unlabeled language-modeling stage on text from the target task or domain before supervised transfer.

ideas.name: Three-stage language-model transfer
ideas.description: A general-domain language model is pretrained, adapted with the target task's unlabeled text, and then converted into a supervised classifier through parameter transfer and controlled fine-tuning.

ideas.name: Discriminative layerwise fine-tuning
ideas.description: Different network layers receive different learning rates during transfer, usually shrinking the rate toward lower layers so generic representations update more cautiously than task-near layers.

ideas.name: Slanted triangular learning rates
ideas.description: A short linear learning-rate rise is followed by a longer linear decay, with a ratio controlling the peak relative to the endpoints.

ideas.name: Gradual layer unfreezing
ideas.description: Transferred layers are unfrozen cumulatively from the task output downward rather than exposing the entire pretrained stack to classifier gradients immediately.

ideas.name: Concat-pooled recurrent document classification
ideas.description: A recurrent document encoder concatenates its final state with temporal maximum and mean pools, exposing endpoint and distributed evidence to the classifier.

ideas.name: BPT3C long-document classification
ideas.description: Long documents are split into fixed-length recurrent batches whose states are carried forward and collected for pooling, while classifier gradients traverse only the batches that contributed to the pooled representation.

ideas.name: Decoder-only Transformer language modeling
ideas.description: A causally masked stack of Transformer blocks maps prior-token embeddings plus a position representation to a next-token distribution without a separate source encoder or encoder-decoder attention path.

ideas.name: Generative Transformer pretraining
ideas.description: A causal Transformer is initialized by maximizing next-token log likelihood over a large unlabeled corpus before its parameters are transferred to labeled target tasks.

ideas.name: Discriminative full-model fine-tuning
ideas.description: Pretrained language-model parameters and a small task output layer are jointly updated on labeled examples rather than keeping the pretrained network fixed as a feature extractor.

ideas.name: Task-aware input serialization
ideas.description: Structured supervised inputs are converted into delimiter-marked token sequences that one pretrained causal model can process with minimal task-specific architectural change.

ideas.name: Auxiliary language-model fine-tuning objective
ideas.description: Supervised fine-tuning adds a weighted causal language-model likelihood on the target sequences to the task-label objective.

ideas.name: Zero-shot generative task probes
ideas.description: Task-specific likelihood rules probe whether an unfine-tuned generative language model can score acceptability, sentiment, candidate answers, or pronoun resolutions.

uncertainties.note: These probes are heterogeneous heuristics with normalized learning curves, not a shared prompt interface or a claim of supervised-level performance.

ideas.name: Byte-pair subword tokenization
ideas.description: A byte-pair encoding process constructs token units through repeated merge operations, giving the language model a fixed subword inventory rather than a word-only vocabulary.

uncertainties.note: The paper specifies 40,000 BPE merges; this is not restated as an exact final vocabulary size.

ideas.name: Deep bidirectional Transformer pretraining
ideas.description: An encoder stack is pretrained with unrestricted self-attention so each token state at every layer may condition jointly on left and right input context; selected targets must be hidden or corrupted to prevent trivial self-copying.

uncertainties.note: The idea names BERT's within-layer bidirectional conditioning and does not reuse ELMo's bidirectional-language-model idea, whose two directions have separate autoregressive objectives and are concatenated only at transfer time.

ideas.name: Masked-language-model pretraining
ideas.description: Select a subset of input tokens, corrupt some of their visible identities, and train a bidirectional encoder to classify each selected token's original vocabulary identity from the surrounding sequence.

uncertainties.note: Only selected positions receive masked-token targets; the objective is not a normalized left-to-right likelihood over every sequence token.

ideas.name: Next-sentence-prediction pretraining
ideas.description: Given packed spans A and B, classify whether B actually follows A in the source corpus or was sampled randomly, using an aggregate sequence representation.

uncertainties.note: The idea records the paper's balanced actual-next/random construction without generalizing its utility beyond the reported BERT recipe and tasks.

ideas.name: Packed text-pair self-attention
ideas.description: Place one or two spans in a single token sequence with separator and segment-identity embeddings so unrestricted self-attention performs joint encoding and cross-span interaction in the same stack.

uncertainties.note: Packing jointly encodes a bounded pair; it does not imply that segment embeddings alone implement cross-attention or that arbitrary numbers of documents are represented.

ideas.name: Fixed-segment context fragmentation
ideas.description: Training a language model on independent fixed-length segments blocks information at artificial boundaries, shortens the context available to early positions, and can force repeated computation when evaluation windows overlap.

uncertainties.note: The problem statement is scoped to the independently segmented Transformer-language-model baseline studied in the paper, not every possible Transformer training or inference implementation.

ideas.name: Segment-level hidden-state recurrence
ideas.description: A later text segment attends to a bounded cache of earlier layer activations so information can cross artificial segment boundaries without recomputing the entire prefix.

uncertainties.note: Recurrence names cross-segment activation reuse; it does not imply a recurrent cell, learned external storage, or backpropagation through the full cached history.

ideas.name: Detached recurrent memory
ideas.description: Cached activations are treated as constant memory for the next segment: they supply keys and values, while gradients remain confined to the current segment's computation graph.

uncertainties.note: A longer forward receptive path does not create an equally long gradient path because the cache is stop-gradient.

ideas.name: Relative-positional self-attention
ideas.description: Attention scores combine content similarity with query-to-key distance, preserving order through relative offsets rather than requiring absolute position indices; a model may use this mechanism with or without cached cross-segment states.

uncertainties.note: The paper's relative vectors are fixed sinusoidal distance encodings combined with learned projections and biases, not a learned lookup table for relative positions.

ideas.name: Relative-shift computation
ideas.description: Project the M+L unique relative-distance vectors once, multiply current queries by that shared projection matrix, then left-shift the resulting score rows into query-specific distance order.

uncertainties.note: The procedure reduces the relative-position projection calculation; it does not remove the quadratic query-by-context score matrix of dense attention.

ideas.name: Relative effective context length
ideas.description: Measure how far added context keeps improving a model relative to a shared short-context baseline, optionally emphasizing difficult positions, and stop when the next increment yields less than a chosen gain threshold.

uncertainties.note: RECL depends on model grouping, difficult-token fraction, context step, shared baseline, and threshold; it is not a literal memory span or a dataset's average dependency length.

ideas.name: Natural-language task conditioning
ideas.description: Represent a task, its input, and its desired output as text so an autoregressive language model can be steered by instructions, formatting, or demonstrations without changing its parameters.

uncertainties.note: The report's evaluations use heterogeneous task strings, examples, filters, candidate scoring, and decoding procedures rather than one standardized instruction interface.

ideas.name: Zero-shot generative task transfer
ideas.description: Evaluate a pretrained causal language model on downstream tasks through textual conditioning and likelihood or generation rules without task-specific parameter updates.

uncertainties.note: Zero-shot is source terminology for no task-specific training or model modification; it does not consistently mean no task demonstrations or no task-specific inference procedure.

ideas.name: WebText pretraining-corpus construction
ideas.description: Use community endorsement of outbound web links as a document-selection signal, then extract, filter, deduplicate, and clean linked pages for language-model pretraining.

uncertainties.note: The corpus consists of linked page text rather than Reddit comments, and community link selection does not convey reuse rights over the linked documents.

ideas.name: Byte-level byte-pair tokenization
ideas.description: Begin with UTF-8 byte symbols and apply constrained byte-pair merges so one finite vocabulary can encode any Unicode string without an unknown-token fallback.

uncertainties.note: The base symbols encode bytes, while merged vocabulary items may span multiple bytes; calling every item a word or one raw byte would be inaccurate.

ideas.name: Model scale and zero-shot transfer
ideas.description: Across four related configurations trained on the same corpus, larger causal language models often improve task-conditioned behavior before matching their own training distribution, while individual metrics can remain weak or nonmonotonic.

uncertainties.note: The four-size comparison is not a compute-matched scaling law, and the reported task matrix contains nonmonotonic steps and weak absolute results.

ideas.name: Permutation language-model pretraining
ideas.description: Maximize token likelihood under sampled factorization orders while leaving the observed token sequence in natural order, so positions can use left and right context across training orders without masked input symbols.

uncertainties.note: The permutation applies to factorization and attention visibility, not to the order of input tokens.

ideas.name: Target-aware two-stream self-attention
ideas.description: Maintain content states that may encode their token and query states that identify a target position without exposing its content, using factorization-specific attention masks to prevent target leakage.

ideas.name: Partial permutation prediction
ideas.description: Sample a factorization order but predict only its final fraction of positions, reducing optimization cost while preserving varied contextual visibility.

ideas.name: Span-based permutation targets
ideas.description: Select contiguous runs of positions as prediction targets inside a wider permutation context, sampling each target span's length while other factorization positions supply context.

ideas.name: Relative segment attention
ideas.description: Encode whether two positions belong to the same or different input segment inside attention scores, replacing absolute segment identities with head-specific relative segment terms.

ideas.name: Dynamic masked-language-model corruption
ideas.description: Regenerate masked-token corruption when an example is presented instead of storing one finite set of static masks, increasing corruption diversity during longer training.

uncertainties.note: RoBERTa's controlled results are mixed and do not support a universal accuracy advantage over static masking.

ideas.name: NSP-free full-sentence packing
ideas.description: Pack full sentences into training blocks of at most 512 tokens and optimize masked-token prediction without next-sentence prediction, optionally crossing document boundaries for regular batch shapes.

uncertainties.note: RoBERTa changes packing together with NSP removal, so the paper does not isolate the loss alone.

ideas.name: Masked-language-model training recipe sensitivity
ideas.description: Model quality attributed to a pretraining family can depend materially on corruption refresh, packing, optimization, batch size, sequence schedule, corpus composition, and training duration.

uncertainties.note: The cumulative RoBERTa recipe does not identify one change as the sole cause of the final gain.

ideas.name: Unified text-to-text task interface
ideas.description: Represent heterogeneous language tasks as text inputs paired with text targets so one encoder–decoder, loss, vocabulary, and decoding interface can serve classification, regression-as-text, question answering, summarization, and translation.

uncertainties.note: The interface unifies representation and training machinery; it does not make task metrics, data conditions, or inference procedures interchangeable.

ideas.name: Scalar bucketed relative-position bias
ideas.description: Add a learned, head-specific scalar to each self-attention logit according to a logarithmically bucketed query–key offset, sharing those bias parameters across layers while collapsing sufficiently large distances into common buckets.

uncertainties.note: T5 does not ablate every architectural deviation from the original Transformer, so the paper does not isolate this bias as the cause of downstream gains.

ideas.name: Sentinel-delimited span reconstruction
ideas.description: Replace each selected input span with an example-unique sentinel and train an autoregressive decoder to emit the removed spans in order, separated by matching sentinels, concentrating target computation on corrupted content; the paper additionally specifies a final unmatched sentinel, while launch code ends the constructed target with EOS instead.

uncertainties.note: The paper prose and Figure 2 require a final unmatched sentinel, while launch preprocessing produces one sentinel per missing span and then appends EOS; the corpus preserves this paper–code conflict.

ideas.name: Heuristically filtered web-corpus pipeline
ideas.description: Turn a fixed web crawl into language-model examples through extraction, language identification, page and line quality filters, term-based exclusions, URL handling, and duplicate-text removal, with the corpus identity depending on the pinned pipeline version as well as the raw crawl.

uncertainties.note: No immutable prepared C4 1.0.0 payload or final-output digest was identified.
uncertainties.resolutionCondition: A versioned prepared-corpus manifest and fully pinned generation environment are required for byte-identical reconstruction.

ideas.name: Mixed supervised and unsupervised pretraining
ideas.description: Pretrain one text-to-text model on a controlled mixture of unlabeled denoising examples and labeled downstream-task examples before performing task-specific fine-tuning.

uncertainties.note: The original final T5 checkpoints include supervised downstream data; later C4-only checkpoint families are separate artifacts.

ideas.name: Transfer recipe and scale composition
ideas.description: Transfer quality can reflect the joint contribution of architecture, objective, corpus quality and repetition, task mixing, fine-tuning, parameter count, training duration, batch size, and ensembling rather than one named technique.

uncertainties.note: T5's controlled rows support scoped comparisons, while its final system changes several factors together and does not identify a single sufficient cause.

ideas.name: Non-embedding parameter and compute accounting
ideas.description: Define model scale with vocabulary and positional embeddings excluded, then estimate forward-plus-backward training work as approximately six floating-point operations per non-embedding parameter per token while keeping omitted context-dependent terms explicit.

uncertainties.note: The definition is source-specific: it omits embeddings, biases, other sub-leading terms, and context-dependent attention work, so it is not interchangeable with total parameter count or measured hardware FLOPs.

ideas.name: Bidirectional–autoregressive sequence denoising
ideas.description: A corrupted sequence is read with bidirectional self-attention and reconstructed by a source-conditioned left-to-right decoder, joining whole-input understanding to autoregressive generation in one pretrained model.

ideas.name: Full-sequence denoising reconstruction
ideas.description: Training predicts every token of the original sequence from a corrupted input, so loss covers intact as well as damaged positions and supports corruptions that change sequence length.

ideas.name: Span infilling with hidden length
ideas.description: Sampled spans are replaced by one mask symbol irrespective of span length, requiring reconstruction of both the missing content and how many tokens were removed; zero-length spans act as insertions.

ideas.name: Sentence-permutation denoising
ideas.description: A document-level corruption shuffles sentence order before reconstruction, testing whether the model can recover discourse-scale ordering rather than only local token content.

ideas.name: Target-side monolingual sequence transfer
ideas.description: A pretrained monolingual encoder–decoder is reused on the target side of translation by attaching a new source encoder, first training the interface while most pretrained parameters stay fixed and then tuning the complete system.

ideas.name: Denoising-objective task dependence
ideas.description: No pretraining corruption dominates every evaluation: objective rankings change between extractive understanding and multiple generation tasks, and multi-factor replicas limit causal interpretation.

ideas.name: Autoregressive Transformer loss scaling
ideas.description: Within a measured decoder-only Transformer and WebText2 regime, cross-entropy loss follows approximate bottleneck-conditioned power laws in non-embedding parameter count, dataset tokens, and batch-adjusted training compute.

uncertainties.note: The finding concerns cross-entropy in the paper's measured family and does not establish universal architecture, capability, downstream-task, tokenizer, or present-day compute-optimal scaling.

ideas.name: Finite-data overfitting scaling
ideas.description: Early-stopped loss and detectable overfitting can be modeled jointly as a function of model size and dataset tokens, separating data-limited from parameter-limited regimes under a fixed regularization procedure.

uncertainties.note: The paper's D∝N^0.74 overfitting-avoidance relation is not its compute-efficient one-epoch allocation, and the smallest-data regime is poorly fit.

ideas.name: Critical batch-size scaling
ideas.description: Estimate a loss-dependent batch scale that trades serial steps against processed examples, then use it to distinguish observed fixed-batch compute from minimum-compute and minimum-step counterfactuals.

uncertainties.note: The critical-batch fit is measured on a narrow model subset and is especially uncertain outside the observed loss range; it is an adjustment model, not a guarantee about arbitrary hardware throughput.

ideas.name: Compute-efficient model and data allocation
ideas.description: Under a fixed non-embedding training-compute and cross-entropy objective, allocate increasing budget across model parameters, critical batch, serial steps, and one-epoch data according to fitted exponents rather than scaling every resource equally.

uncertainties.note: The historical prescription minimizes estimated non-embedding training compute for loss; it excludes inference, hardware, energy, and lifecycle costs, and later compute-optimal revisions require separate evidence.

ideas.name: Inverse-cloze retriever pretraining
ideas.description: Use one sentence as a pseudo-query, its surrounding text as a positive passage, and other batch passages as negatives to initialize semantic retrieval before downstream answer supervision.

ideas.name: Latent answer-derivation marginalization
ideas.description: Normalize joint scores over retrieved evidence blocks and candidate answer spans, then sum the probability of derivations whose span text matches the observed answer.

ideas.name: Retriever–reader open-domain question answering
ideas.description: Use a corpus-scale retriever to expose a bounded candidate set, then a more expensive passage-and-span reader to score answers within those candidates while keeping the two scoring roles explicit.

ideas.name: Dense dual-encoder document retrieval
ideas.description: Encode a query and each candidate passage independently, rank candidates by vector similarity, and use a maximum-inner-product index or equivalent search layer to expose a small retrieved set.

ideas.name: Retrieval-conditioned latent-document marginalization
ideas.description: Treat the retrieved passage as a discrete latent variable and approximate the output likelihood by summing passage-conditioned predictions over a truncated top-k retrieval distribution.

ideas.name: Parametric and non-parametric memory composition
ideas.description: Combine knowledge stored in model parameters with a separately replaceable text corpus or index whose retrieved contents condition prediction.

ideas.name: Retrieval-augmented language-model pretraining
ideas.description: Train a language model and retriever jointly so masked-token likelihood supplies a learning signal for selecting external passages without passage-relevance labels.

ideas.name: Salient-span masked retrieval pretraining
ideas.description: Mask a named entity or date so predicting the missing span encourages retrieval of passages containing useful factual context.

ideas.name: Asynchronous document-index refresh
ideas.description: Recompute document embeddings and rebuild a retrieval index in parallel with model training, accepting bounded staleness between refreshes and rescoring selected candidates with current parameters.

ideas.name: Answer-supervised dense passage retrieval
ideas.description: Train decomposable question and passage encoders from passages matched to gold contexts or selected because they contain an answer string, without requiring manual passage-relevance labels.

ideas.name: In-batch negative retriever training
ideas.description: Reuse the positive passage paired with every other question in a batch as a contrastive negative, turning a B-pair batch into a B-by-B score matrix without separately encoding B times as many negatives.

ideas.name: BM25 hard-negative mining
ideas.description: Select lexically plausible high-ranked passages that lack a recognized answer as difficult contrastive negatives, while retaining the possibility that answer matching can mislabel relevant passages.

ideas.name: Retrieval-augmented sequence generation
ideas.description: Condition an autoregressive generator on retrieved passages and optimize output likelihood after marginalizing the retrieved document variable.

ideas.name: Sequence-level document marginalization
ideas.description: Choose a latent retrieved passage for an entire target sequence and sum the complete sequence probability over the truncated retrieval distribution.

ideas.name: Token-level document marginalization
ideas.description: Marginalize the retrieved passage separately inside each next-token probability so different documents may support different output positions.

ideas.name: Retrieval-index hot swapping
ideas.description: Replace the external retrieval corpus or index at inference time while retaining model parameters, enabling narrowly scoped knowledge updates whose success still depends on retrieval and reader behavior.

ideas.name: Retrieval collapse
ideas.description: A retrieval-augmented generator can converge to nearly input-invariant retrieved passages that the generator ignores, defeating the intended grounding path.

ideas.name: Alternating dense and local sparse attention
ideas.description: Alternate full attention with locally banded sparse attention across decoder layers so a scaled causal language-model stack does not use the same dense attention pattern at every layer.

uncertainties.note: The paper names the alternating pattern and cites Sparse Transformer but does not release an executable layer-by-layer implementation or a controlled ablation isolating it.

ideas.name: Quality-weighted web-corpus mixture
ideas.description: Filter, probabilistically resample, and deduplicate a large web crawl, then combine it with more heavily sampled curated web, books, and encyclopedia sources for language-model training.

uncertainties.note: The disclosed method does not identify the exact crawl-shard list, classifier implementation, prepared-corpus digest, books corpora, or Wikipedia snapshot.
uncertainties.resolutionCondition: Immutable corpus and preprocessing manifests are required for exact reconstruction and rights review.

ideas.name: Demonstration-conditioned in-context learning
ideas.description: Specify a task at inference time through an instruction and zero, one, or several input-output demonstrations placed in the token context, without changing model parameters.

uncertainties.note: Observed adaptation does not by itself identify whether a model learns a new task in context or recognizes and conditions a behavior represented during pretraining.
uncertainties.resolutionCondition: Mechanistic and controlled data-intervention evidence is required to distinguish those explanations by task.

ideas.name: Scale-dependent in-context learning
ideas.description: Across a fixed family of autoregressive models, the gap between zero-, one-, and few-shot behavior often grows with scale, while individual tasks remain weak, nonmonotonic, prompt-sensitive, or split-dependent.

uncertainties.note: The result is an aggregate pattern across the reported family, not a universal emergence threshold or a controlled attribution to parameter count alone.

ideas.name: Benchmark-overlap contamination audit
ideas.description: Search pretraining text for normalized benchmark n-grams, define dirty and clean evaluation subsets, and compare their scores while retaining false-positive, distribution-shift, and incomplete-filtering limits.

uncertainties.note: Small clean/all score differences cannot prove absence of memorization, and the paper's bug, heuristic matches, and shifted subsets prevent a complete causal correction.

ideas.name: Conditional-generation human detection study
ideas.description: Measure whether readers can distinguish conditionally generated news continuations from matched human articles under a fixed sampling, article-length, recruitment, and exclusion procedure.

uncertainties.note: The measured error applies to the paper's news prompts, sampling settings, lengths, and participant pool, not arbitrary generated text or real-world detection systems.

ideas.name: Prompt-conditioned representation bias probing
ideas.description: Probe generated continuations and word associations under demographic prompts to expose representation patterns while keeping prompt choice, sentiment tools, sample size, and normative interpretation explicit.

uncertainties.note: These probes are preliminary measurements under selected prompts and cannot establish a complete fairness profile or a monotonic relationship between scale and social bias.

ideas.name: Reported compute versus measured energy
ideas.description: Keep estimated training FLOPs and PF-days separate from measured electricity, carbon, and lifecycle impact, and do not let a narrow inference-energy estimate substitute for the missing measurements.

uncertainties.note: The paper supplies estimated compute and one order-of-magnitude inference example, not measured training energy, carbon emissions, or a lifecycle assessment.

ideas.name: Human-evaluated summary quality
ideas.description: Treat informed human judgments of accuracy, coverage, coherence, and overall usefulness as the target for abstractive summarization while keeping evaluator instructions, output length, domain, and reference quality explicit.

ideas.name: Supervised demonstration fine-tuning
ideas.description: Update a pretrained causal language model on human-written task demonstrations so it produces a useful initial policy before preference modeling or policy optimization.

ideas.name: Human preference comparison data
ideas.description: Collect pairwise choices or within-prompt rankings over model outputs so relative judgments can supervise a preference predictor without requiring a handcrafted scalar quality metric.

ideas.name: Learned human-preference reward model
ideas.description: Fit a scalar model whose reward differences predict which response a human evaluator prefers, then use that learned proxy for evaluation or policy optimization.

ideas.name: KL-regularized preference policy optimization
ideas.description: Optimize a language-model policy against learned preference reward while penalizing log-probability divergence from a supervised reference policy to limit mode collapse and unsupported reward extrapolation.

ideas.name: Reward-model over-optimization
ideas.description: Policy search can exploit errors in a learned reward proxy so predicted reward continues rising after fresh human preference plateaus or declines.

ideas.name: Multitask supervised instruction tuning
ideas.description: Update a pretrained language model on a heterogeneous supervised mixture whose inputs verbalize task intent, so one post-trained model can be evaluated on excluded task families without task-specific parameter updates at inference.

ideas.name: Prompt-template mixture conditioning
ideas.description: Render each supervised dataset through multiple natural-language input and target templates, sampling across wordings and sometimes task inversions so training does not bind a dataset to one prompt surface form.

uncertainties.note: A larger public prompt pool is not identical to the subset and prompt filters used in any one training mixture.

ideas.name: Task-family held-out generalization
ideas.description: Evaluate transfer by excluding labeled datasets from a declared task family during post-training, while retaining explicit guards for overlapping taxonomies, pretraining exposure, and variant-specific leakage.

uncertainties.note: Held out from supervised post-training does not imply absent from language-model pretraining or absent as a latent skill in another training task.

ideas.name: Instruction-tuning scale dependence
ideas.description: In one related decoder-only model family, the same instruction-mixture intervention improves held-out tasks at roughly hundred-billion-parameter scale but can reduce them at eight billion parameters and below.

uncertainties.note: The result is a family-specific ablation, not a universal scaling law or proof that parameter count alone causes instruction generalization.

ideas.name: Prompt-distribution robustness evaluation
ideas.description: Treat prompt wording as an evaluation distribution and report central tendency plus dispersion across all eligible templates instead of selecting one favorable prompt on held-out labels.

uncertainties.note: Median and interquartile range across a finite contributed prompt set do not measure robustness to every valid instruction.

ideas.name: Public prompt-pool materialization
ideas.description: Maintain community-authored input and target templates with task metadata, then materialize eligible source datasets into prompted examples for reproducible multitask training and evaluation.

uncertainties.note: Tooling, template code, materialized examples, source datasets, and trained checkpoints have separate provenance and license scopes.

ideas.name: Answer-choice likelihood ranking
ideas.description: Score each allowed textual answer under a generative model and predict the option with highest target-sequence likelihood, with results sensitive to candidate formulation and normalization choices.

uncertainties.note: T0 uses unnormalized option likelihood, so this evaluation is distinct from free generation and can favor shorter answer strings.

ideas.name: RMS-normalized autoregressive Transformer
ideas.description: Scale a causal Transformer language model while replacing LayerNorm with RMSNorm and retaining explicit bounds around the rest of the inherited decoder architecture.

ideas.name: SentencePiece tokenization with byte fallback
ideas.description: Tokenize text with a fixed SentencePiece subword vocabulary while falling back to bytes for open-vocabulary coverage, keeping normalization loss and tokenizer identity explicit.

uncertainties.note: Open-vocabulary byte fallback does not make the paper's NFKC preprocessing lossless; superscript and other compatibility distinctions can still collapse.

ideas.name: Large-scale low-precision training
ideas.description: Reduce large-model memory and training cost with bfloat16 parameters and activations while testing whether stochastic rounding or a full-precision master copy preserves small optimizer updates.

uncertainties.note: The controlled master-weight comparison is reported at 417M parameters, not as a repeated 280B Gopher run.

ideas.name: Distributed dense-Transformer training
ideas.description: Fit a dense Transformer and its optimizer state across accelerators with data and model parallelism, rematerialization, state partitioning, and an explicit pipeline or pipeline-free topology across larger hardware groups.

ideas.name: Practical training-compute accounting
ideas.description: Report implementation-aware training and evaluation FLOPs, accelerator-time decomposition, and carbon-estimate inputs while naming omitted development, pre-emption, and operational work.

uncertainties.note: A best-effort implementation-aware lower bound is not directly interchangeable with a theoretical six-parameter-token FLOP estimate or total project energy.

ideas.name: MassiveText corpus pipeline
ideas.description: Build a multi-source English corpus with source-specific sampling, heuristic web filtering, repetition removal, near-duplicate controls, test-overlap filtering, and fixed-length example construction.

uncertainties.note: The paper does not provide an immutable prepared-corpus manifest, preprocessing implementation, full source-level rights record, or final payload digest.
uncertainties.resolutionCondition: A versioned data and preprocessing release with provenance, rights, and payload hashes is required.

ideas.name: Fixed-token capability-scaling profile
ideas.description: Compare related autoregressive models trained for the same token count across a broad task matrix, preserving nonuniform gains, changed training regimes, heterogeneous metrics, and negative cases.

uncertainties.note: Holding token count and corpus family fixed does not isolate parameter count because architecture dimensions, optimizer settings, batch size, precision, and training compute also change.

ideas.name: Relative-position context extrapolation
ideas.description: Evaluate beyond a trained context window by clamping relative-distance features at the training limit, gaining usable context for some domains while collapsing all farther distances into one position class.

ideas.name: Prompt-conditioned raw-model dialogue
ideas.description: Turn a raw autoregressive language model into a conversational interface by placing a hand-written persona and example turns in context, without treating format compliance as factuality or safety training.

ideas.name: Scale-dependent toxicity and distributional bias
ideas.description: Measure how prompted toxicity, unprompted generations, toxicity classification, stereotypes, sentiment associations, and dialect likelihood vary with model scale under explicitly limited classifiers and templates.

uncertainties.note: Classifier scores and selected templates are partial, culturally contingent measurements rather than a complete fairness or harm profile.

ideas.name: Labeler-scoped instruction alignment
ideas.description: Train responses toward inferred user intent under helpfulness, truthfulness, and harmlessness guidance while explicitly treating the result as preferences of a particular labeler, researcher, prompt, and deployment context rather than universal human values.

ideas.name: Pretraining-mix-regularized policy optimization
ideas.description: Accumulate a weighted next-token likelihood gradient from pretraining-distribution text alongside PPO gradients to reduce capability regressions during preference optimization.

ideas.name: Fixed-compute model and data allocation
ideas.description: Given a fixed training-FLOP budget, choose a parameter count and training-token count that minimize fitted autoregressive loss while keeping compute conventions and the measured regime explicit.

uncertainties.note: The promoted object is a bounded loss-minimization problem under training compute, not a universal optimum over serving cost, latency, memory, energy, data rights, or downstream utility.

ideas.name: Schedule-matched training horizon
ideas.description: Fit or compare a model at a target token horizon using a learning-rate schedule designed for that horizon rather than treating an intermediate point on a longer decay schedule as equivalent.

uncertainties.note: The paper shows schedule dependence and proposes it as one contributor to disagreement with Kaplan; it does not isolate every methodological cause.

ideas.name: Training-curve envelope scaling
ideas.description: For each compute budget, form a loss envelope across complete training curves, smooth the budget-wise minima, and fit power laws for the model and token coordinates of the frontier.

ideas.name: IsoFLOP profile scaling
ideas.description: At each fixed compute budget, compare final loss across model sizes, locate the profile minimum, and fit how its parameter and token coordinates move as compute grows.

ideas.name: Parametric model-data loss surface
ideas.description: Fit an irreducible-loss term plus separate inverse power laws in parameters and tokens, then minimize the fitted surface along a fixed-compute constraint.

uncertainties.note: The additive power-law form is a fitted premise with visible high-compute curvature, not a mechanistic decomposition proven outside the sampled family.

ideas.name: Near-balanced parameter and token scaling
ideas.description: Within the paper's dense autoregressive-Transformer regime, the compute-optimal parameter and token coordinates grow at similar powers of training compute rather than assigning most marginal compute to parameters.

uncertainties.note: Near-balanced exponents do not establish an architecture-independent constant tokens-per-parameter rule.

ideas.name: Compute-matched Chinchilla validation
ideas.description: Train a smaller Gopher-derived model on substantially more tokens at approximately the same training FLOPs, then compare language-model loss and downstream task results with protocol and confound boundaries intact.

uncertainties.note: The large-scale comparison validates one selected configuration, not every projected point, and changes optimizer, tokenizer normalization, batch schedule, and sample mixture as well as parameter and token counts.

ideas.name: MassiveText mixture training
ideas.description: Sample a disclosed mixture of filtered web pages, books, C4, news, code, and Wikipedia at source-specific weights and aggregate repeat rates while retaining the proprietary-data boundary.

uncertainties.note: The composition table does not expose an immutable corpus manifest, prepared examples, source-level rights, filtering code, or deduplication artifacts.
uncertainties.resolutionCondition: A versioned training-data and preprocessing release with rights metadata is required.

ideas.name: Training versus inference model size
ideas.description: A smaller model trained on more tokens can use a fixed training budget effectively while reducing per-token serving cost, but the paper does not optimize or measure a complete inference workload.

uncertainties.note: The serving advantage is inferred from parameter count; latency, throughput, memory traffic, hardware utilization, energy, and lifecycle cost are not measured.

ideas.name: SwiGLU Transformer feed-forward layer
ideas.description: Use a gated SwiGLU intermediate transformation in each causal Transformer block while keeping the extra matrix multiplication and comparison baseline explicit.

ideas.name: Parallel attention–MLP Transformer block
ideas.description: Apply attention and the feed-forward path in parallel to the same normalized input, then add both outputs to the residual stream so their large matrix multiplications can be fused.

uncertainties.note: PaLM reports a small 8B ablation cost and no 62B cost, then extrapolates quality neutrality at 540B rather than running a controlled 540B ablation.

ideas.name: Multi-query attention
ideas.description: Retain one query projection per attention head while sharing key and value projections across heads to reduce cached state and accelerator work during autoregressive decoding.

ideas.name: Rotary position embeddings
ideas.description: Encode token position by rotating query and key channels as a function of position instead of adding an absolute or relative position vector to token representations.

ideas.name: Pipeline-free multi-pod data parallelism
ideas.description: Shard a dense model within each accelerator pod, replicate the sharded model across pods, and exchange gradients between pods without introducing pipeline stages.

ideas.name: Model FLOPs utilization
ideas.description: Compare achieved token throughput with the theoretical peak throughput implied by model-required forward and backward FLOPs, while stating whether attention and rematerialization work enter the numerator or denominator.

ideas.name: Z-loss-stabilized autoregressive training
ideas.description: Add a small squared log-partition penalty to next-token log loss to discourage excessively large logits while preserving the main autoregressive objective.

ideas.name: Multilingual text-and-code mixture pretraining
ideas.description: Pretrain one decoder on a weighted mixture of multilingual web, conversation, books, encyclopedic text, news, and repository-license-filtered source code while retaining language, filtering, provenance, and distribution limits.

ideas.name: Coarse-scale discontinuity audit
ideas.description: Project a task's largest-scale score from its two smaller-scale scores and record the residual, while treating three model sizes without repeats or uncertainty bands as a descriptive screen rather than a mechanistic threshold test.

ideas.name: Few-shot chain-of-thought prompting
ideas.description: Place worked intermediate-reasoning exemplars in the inference context and score only the produced answer, keeping prompt authorship, calculator use, comparators, and faithfulness unbundled.

ideas.name: Exact-continuation memorization audit
ideas.description: Prompt with the opening of sampled training spans, greedily decode the continuation, and stratify exact matches by model scale and span duplication without equating the result to untargeted extraction risk.

ideas.name: Refreshed-data continued pretraining
ideas.description: Resume a checkpoint for additional tokens using refreshed data and a revised mixture, then compare repeated-data and refreshed-data controls before attributing the resulting capability change.

ideas.name: Cross-corpus MinHash deduplication
ideas.description: Compare documents across a combined training collection with approximate MinHash locality-sensitive hashing and remove pairs above a declared Jaccard threshold, while retaining the limits of approximate similarity and undisclosed preprocessing.

ideas.name: Mid-flight large-run recovery
ideas.description: Recover an unstable long-running training job by selecting an earlier healthy checkpoint and changing optimization or infrastructure settings, while recording that the final run is no longer one clean controlled recipe.

ideas.name: Training-run operational logbook
ideas.description: Publish dated incident, restart, diagnostic, and intervention records from a large training run so operational decisions and human overhead can be audited alongside the final model description.

ideas.name: Research-gated model-weight release
ideas.description: Distribute some checkpoints directly while placing the largest weights behind eligibility review and non-commercial terms, keeping availability, access procedure, permitted use, and open-source code as separate properties.

ideas.name: Public model-scale ladder
ideas.description: Release related checkpoints at multiple parameter scales so researchers can compare behaviors across a family, while preserving differences in training runs, data exposure, and artifact completeness.

ideas.name: Benchmark-scoped model harm profiling
ideas.description: Profile one declared model or access surface with toxicity, stereotype, hate-speech, and unsafe-dialogue benchmarks while preserving prompt, decoding, classifier, comparator, language, and construct-validity limits instead of generalizing to comprehensive safety or causal data effects.

ideas.name: Participatory multilingual source curation
ideas.description: A corpus-building process in which language communities help choose sources and set processing thresholds, making language expertise part of data construction rather than a post-hoc evaluation layer.

ideas.name: Source-traceable composite data governance
ideas.description: A release and stewardship scheme that keeps corpus components identifiable so access and reuse decisions can reflect the source's licenses, custodians, privacy risk, and agreements instead of inheriting one umbrella label.

ideas.name: Language-specific web-document filtering
ideas.description: A web-corpus pipeline whose repetition, character, function-word, flagged-word, perplexity, and length thresholds are selected separately by language with native-speaker review.

ideas.name: Length-split near-duplicate removal
ideas.description: A deduplication pipeline that uses one similarity method for shorter documents and a substring method for long documents after observing length-related false positives.

ideas.name: Limited pattern-based PII redaction
ideas.description: A scalable redaction pass for a bounded set of identifier patterns whose operational simplicity leaves other personal information and consent questions unresolved.

ideas.name: Tokenizer-fertility corpus audit
ideas.description: Using tokens per input byte as a component-level diagnostic for unusual content, possible language or crawl errors, and cross-corpus domain differences while avoiding direct tokenizer quality claims.

ideas.name: ALiBi distance-linear attention-logit bias
ideas.description: Inject head-specific linear distance penalties directly into causal attention logits instead of adding learned or sinusoidal position vectors to token embeddings.

uncertainties.note: BLOOM adopts ALiBi but does not claim its mechanism or long-context motivation as a BigScience contribution.

ideas.name: Embedding LayerNorm stability trade-off
ideas.description: Add normalization immediately after token embeddings to reduce observed large-run instability while retaining the possibility that it degrades zero-shot transfer or becomes unnecessary under a wider numeric format.

ideas.name: Multilingual tokenizer fertility balancing
ideas.description: Design and audit a byte-level subword vocabulary across languages with fertility constraints, lossless encoding, no text normalization, and language-aware pretokenization rather than reusing an English-only tokenizer unchanged.

ideas.name: Checkpoint-level model documentation
ideas.description: Publish model cards, intermediate training states, and operational context at checkpoint granularity so a release can be inspected as an evolving run rather than only as final weights.

ideas.name: Responsible-use-restricted model release
ideas.description: Make model parameters available under terms that grant reuse while prohibiting enumerated behaviors, keeping model, source code, data, and output rights as separate scopes.

ideas.name: Output-truncation-sensitive generation evaluation
ideas.description: Report how generation metrics change when overlong or wrong-language continuations are truncated, so content quality is not silently conflated with stopping behavior.

ideas.name: Interleaved reasoning-action-observation trajectories
ideas.description: Generate visible language traces and task actions in one sequential context, then append environment observations so subsequent tokens can condition on both prior deliberative text and external feedback.

uncertainties.note: The visible textual trace is an interface object and training target; it is not assumed to be a faithful readout of hidden model computation.

ideas.name: Explicit environment query-observation loop
ideas.description: Expose a bounded action vocabulary that can query or change an external environment and serialize the returned observation into the model's next-step context.

ideas.name: Sparse asynchronous reasoning traces
ideas.description: Permit a prompted policy to emit free-form reasoning only at selected points in a long action sequence instead of forcing one thought before every environment action.

ideas.name: Heuristic internal-external reasoning fallback
ideas.description: Switch between self-consistent reasoning-only samples and an environment-acting trajectory when a step limit or low answer agreement indicates that the current route may be unreliable.

ideas.name: Success-filtered trajectory fine-tuning
ideas.description: Use trajectories generated by a larger prompted model only when their final answers pass a task success check, then fine-tune smaller models to decode the retained thought, action, and observation sequences.

uncertainties.note: Outcome filtering does not validate the factuality or faithfulness of every intermediate trace token.

ideas.name: Generated thought-trace editing
ideas.description: Expose generated textual planning traces so a human can revise selected tokens and let later actions condition on the edited context, without changing model parameters.

uncertainties.note: ReAct demonstrates this with one qualitative ALFWorld trajectory rather than a systematic controllability or safety evaluation.

ideas.name: In-context API-call annotation
ideas.description: Use a small demonstration prompt to make a pretrained causal language model propose call positions and textual API arguments inside ordinary language-modeling examples.

uncertainties.note: The demonstrations and tool descriptions are human-authored; self-supervision begins with model sampling and loss-based selection.

ideas.name: Counterfactual future-token tool filtering
ideas.description: Keep an executed tool call when its result lowers a model's weighted loss on nearby future tokens relative to both no call and the same call without a returned result.

uncertainties.note: The score measures usefulness to one scorer on one continuation; it is not a human factuality, safety, or task-value label.

ideas.name: Inline API-call language modeling
ideas.description: Interleave retained textual calls and tool results with their source text, then train the same next-token objective over the augmented sequences.

ideas.name: Inference-time API-result injection
ideas.description: Pause autoregressive decoding at a generated call marker, execute an external text-valued tool, insert its result, and resume generation from the expanded context.

ideas.name: Tool-call rank triggering
ideas.description: Trigger a tool call when the call-start marker appears within a chosen rank of the next-token distribution, trading ordinary model selectivity for a higher call rate.

ideas.name: Model-relative tool utility
ideas.description: Treat a tool's measured benefit as conditional on the base model, tool quality, prompt, task, and call policy rather than as an intrinsic property of external-tool access.

uncertainties.note: The Toolformer evidence compares a small set of model and tool pairings and does not imply a universal ordering of models or tools.

ideas.name: Conditional parameter-capacity scaling
ideas.description: Increase total stored feed-forward capacity by adding expert parameter sets while activating only a routed subset for each token, keeping total parameters distinct from active arithmetic and communication.

uncertainties.note: Total parameter count, active parameters, FLOPs, memory, communication, and elapsed time remain separate accounting axes.

ideas.name: Token-wise top-1 expert routing
ideas.description: Use a learned softmax router to send each token representation to one highest-scoring feed-forward expert and scale that expert's output by its gate probability.

ideas.name: Fixed-capacity expert dispatch
ideas.description: Allocate each expert a static token buffer derived from average load and a capacity factor, padding unused slots and bypassing or rerouting overflow under an explicit policy.

ideas.name: Router load-balancing objective
ideas.description: Penalize the dot product of realized expert-assignment fractions and differentiable mean router probabilities so token traffic approaches uniform use of available experts.

uncertainties.note: Uniform traffic is a systems and optimization objective, not proof of semantic specialization or equal expert value.

ideas.name: Selective router precision
ideas.description: Perform numerically sensitive local router operations in float32, then return dispatch and combine tensors to bfloat16 before cross-device communication.

ideas.name: Expert-only fine-tuning dropout
ideas.description: Apply stronger dropout inside expert feed-forward computations than in shared layers to regularize sparse models during small-task fine-tuning.

ideas.name: Joint data, model, and expert parallelism
ideas.description: Partition batches, dense matrix dimensions, and unique experts across a logical device mesh while accounting separately for all-reduce and all-to-all communication.

ideas.name: Sparse-to-dense teacher distillation
ideas.description: Initialize a compact dense student from shared non-expert weights and mix teacher probabilities with ground-truth targets to retain part of a sparse teacher's quality gain.

ideas.name: Group-relative policy optimization
ideas.description: Sample multiple outputs for each prompt, standardize rewards within that group to estimate relative advantages, and optimize a clipped policy-ratio objective with reference-policy KL control without a separately trained critic.

uncertainties.note: Eliminating the value model reduces one PPO component but not rollout, reward, reference-policy, or distributed-training requirements.

ideas.name: Verifiable-outcome reasoning reward
ideas.description: Reward a generated solution using automatically checked final-answer correctness plus explicit output-format constraints while leaving intermediate reasoning tokens unsupervised.

uncertainties.note: Verifiable outcomes are strongest for tasks with reliable parsers, compilers, tests, or concise reference answers and do not validate every intermediate step.

ideas.name: SFT-free reasoning reinforcement learning
ideas.description: Apply outcome-driven policy optimization directly to a pretrained base checkpoint without an intervening supervised reasoning-trace fine-tuning stage.

uncertainties.note: SFT-free describes the immediate post-training sequence, not the pretrained base model's data provenance or absence of prior reasoning exposure.

ideas.name: Multistage reasoning post-training
ideas.description: Alternate curated supervised traces, verifiable-reward reinforcement learning, rejection-sampled supervised data, and mixed preference/reasoning reinforcement learning to balance reasoning, readability, safety, and general instruction following.

ideas.name: Language-consistency reward
ideas.description: Reward the fraction of response words that match a designated target language to reduce cross-language mixing during reasoning-oriented policy optimization.

uncertainties.note: Surface-language consistency is not semantic correctness, multilingual coverage, or cross-lingual fairness.

ideas.name: Rejection-sampled reasoning-trace fine-tuning
ideas.description: Generate candidate long-form solutions, retain traces that pass correctness and readability filters, mix them with general instruction data, and fine-tune a base model on the curated set.

ideas.name: Reasoning-trace distillation
ideas.description: Supervised-fine-tune a smaller student model on long-form outputs generated by a stronger reasoning teacher while preserving the student's distinct base architecture and rights.

uncertainties.note: Teacher-output transfer is not evidence that the student shares the teacher's architecture, reinforcement-learning history, or internal computation.

ideas.name: Adaptive reasoning-token allocation
ideas.description: Allow a model to vary the number of visible intermediate tokens it generates before a final answer, using more serial generation as a form of test-time computation on some harder prompts.

uncertainties.note: Token count is an observable compute proxy; it is not a direct measure of problem difficulty, useful reasoning, or faithful internal cognition.

ideas.name: Direct preference policy optimization
ideas.description: Fit a language-model policy directly to pairwise preference labels with a logistic objective over policy-versus-reference log-probability ratios, without a separately trained scalar reward network or policy-gradient stage.

ideas.name: Policy–reward log-ratio duality
ideas.description: Rewrite the optimizer of a KL-regularized reward objective as a reference policy exponentially tilted by reward, then recover an equivalent reward from the policy-to-reference log ratio up to a prompt-only constant.

uncertainties.note: The paper's representation theorem assumes a positive reference probability for every prompt–completion pair and beta greater than zero; it is not an unconditional statement about finite neural optimization.

ideas.name: Implicit policy-defined preference reward
ideas.description: Interpret beta times the policy-to-reference log-probability ratio as the representative reward selected from a preference-equivalent class, so the trained policy acts as both generator and implicit reward parameterization.

ideas.name: Offline static-preference policy learning
ideas.description: Optimize a policy from a fixed batch of preferred and dispreferred response pairs without sampling new responses inside the policy-update loop.

uncertainties.note: The preference pairs still originate from earlier model sampling and human or proxy labeling; offline optimization does not remove data-generation or evaluator costs.

ideas.name: Evaluator-dependent preference evidence
ideas.description: Treat measured preference gains as conditional on the evaluator, prompt wording, candidate sampling temperature, reference response, task distribution, and comparison protocol rather than as a universal quality ordering.

claims.statement: The paper frames the Transformer as a sequence-transduction model relying entirely on self-attention for input and output representations without sequence-aligned recurrence or convolution. Its introduction cites Luong et al. only within a group of efforts advancing recurrent language models and encoder–decoder architectures and identifies Parikh et al. among the few attention cases not coupled to recurrence; its background includes Cheng in the prior self-/intra-attention task citation sequence whose first listed context is reading comprehension, includes Parikh in the same sequence alongside textual entailment, cites End-To-End Memory Networks as recurrent attention outside sequence-aligned recurrence, and separately groups ByteNet with convolutional efforts that compute hidden positions in parallel while requiring a logarithmically growing operation path between distant positions. The scaled-dot-product paragraph does not cite Luong, and none of these contextual or contrastive citations states that the Transformer adopts Cheng’s recurrent memory tape, Parikh’s attend–compare–aggregate factorization, or ByteNet’s mask, dilation schedule, stacking, or dynamic unfolding. The same background directly contrasts ConvS2S as a parallel convolutional predecessor with a linear arbitrary-position path; Section 3.2.3 includes it among encoder–decoder attention mechanisms the Transformer cross-attention route mimics, and Section 3.5 tests its cited learned positional-embedding alternative while retaining sinusoidal positions as the canonical default. Those scoped citations support one qualified build-on relationship, not adoption of ConvS2S’s convolution, GLUs, or layerwise hops as the cause of core self-attention. The atlas therefore treats the paper as an architectural convergence point rather than an origin claim for attention, self-attention, dot products, parallel transduction, or autoregressive generation.

claims.statement: ORQA precomputes ICT block embeddings into a maximum-inner-product index and freezes the evidence encoder during QA fine-tuning while updating the question encoder and reader, so query-side changes can alter top-k retrieval without rebuilding document vectors.

claims.statement: WebText2 extends WebText's outbound Reddit links with at least three karma through December 2017 by adding January–October 2018 links under the same threshold and extracting new pages with Newspaper3k. claims.statement: The paper defines N as non-embedding model parameters, excluding vocabulary and positional embeddings, and approximates forward compute as 2N plus a context-dependent attention term. The context-dependent term can cease to be negligible when context length approaches or exceeds roughly twelve times model width.

claims.statement: Unless otherwise noted, runs use 250,000 updates, batches of 512 sequences of 1,024 tokens, Adam, a 3,000-step linear warmup, and cosine decay to zero; models above one billion parameters use Adafactor for memory reasons. claims.statement: REALM decomposes prediction into retrieval followed by passage-conditioned prediction and defines p(y|x) as a sum over latent passages z; the implementation approximates that corpus-wide marginal with the retriever's top-k candidates.

evidence.support: Equation 1 defines the latent-passage marginal and the surrounding text states that training uses a top-k approximation.

limitations: The exact written sum and the implemented truncated approximation are distinct; top-k candidate discovery is itself approximate.

claims.statement: REALM scores passages by the inner product of BERT-style query and document encoders: the document embedder encodes a title-plus-body pair, while a separate Transformer knowledge encoder jointly processes the input and the selected passage body.

evidence.support: The retriever embeds each document's title and body for inner-product scoring; the knowledge encoder separately joins the input with the retrieved passage body.

limitations: The corpus-wide softmax is the model definition; candidate discovery uses approximate maximum-inner-product search.

claims.statement: During pretraining the knowledge encoder predicts masked tokens conditioned on a retrieved passage; during open-QA fine-tuning it assigns probability to contiguous spans and sums scores for spans matching the answer string.

evidence.support: The paper specifies masked-token prediction for pretraining and an extractive span model for open question answering.

limitations: The downstream reader assumes an answer occurs verbatim as a contiguous span; it is not an open-ended generator.

claims.statement: The retriever gradient raises a passage's score when its conditional prediction probability exceeds the current marginal, while training asynchronously rebuilds a stale document index every several hundred steps and rescores selected passages with current parameters.

claims.statement: T0 groups datasets mainly by task format, then holds out NLI, coreference, sentence completion, and word-sense disambiguation: CB, RTE, three ANLI rounds, WSC, Winogrande, COPA, HellaSwag, Story Cloze, and WiC form 11 reported dataset-or-round results. Fourteen selected English, tokenizer-compatible BIG-bench tasks provide a second held-out set.

locator.section: 3 Measuring generalization to held-out tasks; Figure 2

evidence.support: Defines the four groups, evaluation datasets, selection rules, and acknowledged taxonomy heuristic.

limitations: The taxonomy is fuzzy and format-based; Appendix D documents entailment- and coreference-like content crossing the nominal group boundaries.

claims.statement: P3 is reported as 2,073 contributor-written prompts for 177 datasets, using Jinja input and target templates plus answer-choice and metric metadata. Training can include original-task and inverted or non-original prompts, while reported held-out evaluation excludes non-original prompts; T0's experimental subset averages 8.03 eligible templates per training dataset rather than using the whole public pool.

Defines p=1, p=5.7 original-only, and p=8.03 all eligible training templates.

claims.statement: Every T0 variant initializes from encoder-decoder T5+LM: T5 pretraining on one trillion C4 tokens with its masked span-style objective followed by 100 billion additional C4 tokens under standard language modeling. Main variants use 11B parameters, the smaller ablation uses 3B, and prompted fine-tuning maximizes target-token likelihood without reconstructing input tokens.

evidence.support: Names the T5 and LM-adaptation stages, 11B/3B sizes, and autoregressive target likelihood.

limitations: The extra 100B-token LM adaptation is attributed to Lester et al.; the T5 source node covers the base architecture and original pretraining rather than that later checkpoint as a separate work.

claims.statement: T0, T0+, and T0++ use 39, 49, and 55 paper-listed dataset configurations. T0+ adds GPT-3 evaluation datasets; T0++ additionally adds SuperGLUE except RTE and CB, leaving only NLI and BIG-bench held out. Consequently the gray T0+ and T0++ cells for trained-on tasks are not zero-shot results.

evidence.support: Defines which dataset groups T0+ and T0++ add and which tasks remain held out.

evidence.support: Lists 39/49/55 configurations and visually separates trained-on evaluation rows.
